findings.obs_text: Giving follows the thought in Judg 15:2 (the father gave his daughter away because he thought Samson hated her), 1Sa 18:17 and 1Sa 18:21 (Saul gives his daughter thinking to snare David), and Jer 3:19 (the Lord thought to give a pleasant land). In Deu 15:9 the unworthy thought keeps one from giving to the poor, and in Joh 13:29 some think Judas was to give to the poor. In Luk 8:18, Luk 12:51, Rom 12:3, Jer 40:5, Dan 7:25 and Job 32:17 giving names grace given, peace not given, a gift, the saints given over, and Elihu's share; in Job 15:35 and Isa 7:14 birth and sign go with conceive, and in 1Cor 13:11 childish thinking is given up.
findings.grounds: I really thought that you utterly hated her, so I gave her

findings.obs_text: In Isa 59:7 the thoughts are thoughts of iniquity, and in Isa 59:4 mischief is conceived and iniquity born: sin is the content of the thoughts. In Deu 15:9 the unworthy thought that withholds from the poor becomes sin. In Luk 13:2 the hearers are asked whether they think the Galileans were worse sinners, in 1Cor 7:36 the one who thinks he behaves badly does not sin by marrying, and in 1Pe 4:1 the way of thinking armed with goes with ceasing from sin. In Psa 51:5 sin is the state in which the psalmist was conceived.
findings.grounds: their thoughts are thoughts of iniquity

older.finding: The root ḥûl, "to twist, whirl", is rendered as birth: "the God who gave you birth" (Deu 32:18); "I was brought forth in iniquity" (Psa 51:5).
older.reason: it states a face or use of the sin words; the sin collection owns it

older.finding: Aimed at the inner being: "you delight in truth in the inward being, and you teach me wisdom in the secret heart" (Psa 51:6), said by one "brought forth in iniquity" (51:5). His delight looks for truth inside, and he teaches there. The verse also belongs in Ch 4.
older.reason: it states how sin works in a person; the sin collection owns it

findings.obs_text: In Eph 3:20 God is able to do more than we ask or think: his power exceeds the reach of thought.
findings.grounds: far more abundantly than all that we ask or think
